The hotspot can't start without a driver. This app bundles the D-Link/Realtek driver 1.27.831.2023, so no internet or extra software is needed.

ui.beacon.footer:
The beacon is scanned by another Wi-Fi adapter on the PC (usually the built-in Wi-Fi) and shows what the hotspot actually advertises.
The real link rate also depends on the device (Quest 3 supports Wi-Fi 6 / 80 MHz / 2 streams), distance and interference.

ui.maint.optimizeConfirm:
One-click optimize will:
• Turn off "turn off the mobile hotspot when no devices are connected"
• Turn off D-Link power saving (Device Manager power management and the driver's power-saving options) and make sure 802.11ax is enabled
• Power plan: turn off USB selective suspend and set the wireless adapter to maximum performance
• Allow this app through Windows Firewall (UDP 67 etc.)
• Ask whether to set Meta's OVRService to manual start (so it does not grab the D-Link)

The PC's own Wi-Fi stays connected. Continue?
ui.maint.optimizeTip: Turns off hotspot auto-off and D-Link power saving, sets high-performance power options and adds firewall rules (administrator)
ui.maint.repairConfirm:
Repair network will:
1. Turn the hotspot off for a moment (connected devices drop for 10–20 seconds)
2. Check Hyper-V's vEthernet (Default Switch) and ask whether to disable it
3. Remove stale Windows connection sharing (ICS) records that point to adapters that no longer exist
4. Restart the Windows connection sharing service (SharedAccess)
5. Turn the hotspot back on and check who hands out IPs

The PC's own Wi-Fi / Ethernet connection is not interrupted. Continue?
ui.maint.repairFooter: If a device still gets no IP: "forget this network" on the device and reconnect; with security software such as Kaspersky, mark VRAirBridgeHotspot.exe as trusted.
ui.maint.repairTip: Use when devices get no IP or no internet: restarts the hotspot and Windows connection sharing and handles the Hyper-V Default Switch and stale ICS records
ui.maint.revertConfirm:
Revert will:
• Turn the hotspot off
• Delete the WinNAT this app created (VRAirBridgeNat) and the IPv4 forwarding it enabled
• Delete the Wi-Fi profiles the channel pin copied to the D-Link and restore the D-Link's metric (if used)
• Re-enable adapters this app disabled (for example vEthernet (Default Switch))
• Set Meta's OVRService back to automatic start (if it was changed)
• Delete this app's firewall rules and autostart task

Continue?
ui.maint.revertDone: The hotspot is off; click "Start hotspot" to keep using it.
ui.maint.revertFooter:
Afterwards you can simply delete VRAirBridgeHotspot.exe and the config.json, dhcp-leases.json and logs folder next to it.
The Windows Mobile hotspot name/password and adapter power settings are kept.
ui.maint.revertTip: Undo every change this app made to the system (use before uninstalling)
